summary.text: Marci Laffen is the Republican candidate for the Kansas House of Representatives, District 12, in the November 3, 2026 general election, facing Democrat Pete Ferrell; no incumbent is seeking the seat.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she described herself as a nurse, farmland owner and Constitution coach who emphasizes property rights and limited government.

paragraphs.text: Marci Laffen earned a bachelor's degree from Bethel College in 1992, according to Ballotpedia.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she said she grew up working on her family's farm, was a two-sport collegiate athlete, and trained and worked as a nurse.
She said she has been married 33 years, has two adult children, and owns and manages farmland with her sisters and mother.
Laffen advanced unopposed from the August 4, 2026 Republican primary, receiving 3,380 votes.
She said she is a Wallbuilders Constitution Coach and wants eminent domain laws reviewed to give landowners more rights, along with limited and deregulated government and lower taxes.
Her stated policy interests include opposition to abortion, defending traditional marriage, reducing government spending, parental rights and education.
She listed Kansans for Life, Stand for Health Freedom and the Kansas Farm Bureau as endorsers.
